name: Tyler
tagline: Heir. Flipper. Two hundred push-ups a day. Currently, and against his express wishes, the bathroom.
notes: Stats run 0-20 (clamped). Ending thresholds mirror Lukey: stay = romance >= 16 && friction < 8; let him go (loved) = romance >= 16; friends = friendship >= 14 && friction < 8; 'That's your call' gives friends if friction < 8, grumpy if friction >= 8. He says 'ma'am' until Act 4 and uses your real name there if romance >= 12. Cross-character budget: Act 1 mentions nobody; Acts 2-4 have at most two housemate references each, spent on jealousy (v2_rival, v2_pinky / v3_jealous, v3_wyatt|v3_wyatt_spoke / v4_late_lukey, plus the vanity light in the friend_success card). Jealousy openers read lukey/malcolm.talkedtoday and lukey/malcolm.romance (>= 6 in Act 2, >= 10 in Act 3). The dehumidifier is an appliance with no name. Dan only appears in inspection.json on day 30. Sets flag.tyler_no (each time she tells him no), flag.tyler_hal (v2_home) and flag.tyler_video (v3_reveal). Reads flag.lukey_blackout, flag.lukey_human, flag.wyatt_spoke_up and lukey.romance as optional flavour.

romance_success.title: Tile Death Do Us Part
romance_success.text: Tyler stayed. The tile is restored, regrouted and sealed, one cracked square mended with a seam of gold, and he is unbearably proud of it. He still gives orders. You still say no. He does his push-ups at oh-five-hundred and makes you count. He has never been happier.

romance_failure.title: Tile We Meet Again
romance_failure.text: Told no and loved anyway, Tyler finally finished his business. He kissed you, saluted, and was gone. The cracked tile by the tub has a seam of gold in it now. When the morning light hits it, it looks a lot like rose quartz.

friend_success.title: Grout Expectations
friend_success.text: Tyler left a better man than he arrived: restored, regrouted and saluted back at last. He passed on at attention. The vanity light stayed on for a week, at exactly the angle Tyler liked.

friend_failure.title: Grout of Here
friend_failure.text: You kept the tile. Tyler did NOT get his way, and he left furious, deeply moved and refusing to admit either. One tile on the bottom row is very slightly crooked. He did that. Out of spite. It's the best tile in the house.

lines: *The bathroom is pink. Not a little pink. Floor-to-ceiling, 1957, glazed-ceramic PINK. One tile by the tub has a hairline crack.*

*The tile shimmers, and a man steps out of the wall. A very, very large man. Shirtless. From the neck down he IS the wall: glossy hot-pink square tile with crisp white grout lines, flaking into bare skin at the collarbones and wrists.*
*He has a square jaw, blue eyes, a hot-pink pompadour, pink drawstring gym shorts, white crew socks and pink high-tops. He stands like he's waiting for a flag to be raised.*
Ma'am. Thank God. A professional.
Tyler Whitmore. Of the [Whitmores|whitmore]. You'll have seen the towers. Our name's on them. In gold.
You: Whitmore like Whitmore Tower? Downtown?
Whitmore Tower. Whitmore Plaza. Whitmore Grand. Whitmore Parking Structure B. I was raised by nannies, an etiquette coach and Fort Bellamy Military Academy.
It's a lot of gold lettering for one man. I've coped.
And you've bought this house to flip it. Outstanding. I've already drawn up the plan. I drew it up a while ago, before my... [reassignment].
Look at this. LOOK at it. Pepto-Bismol. Floor to ceiling. It's like standing inside a flamingo's mouth.
Rip it out. White. [Subway]. Basic. SELL.

choices.text: Finally. Someone who speaks flipper.
Bold words from a man with pink hair.
Actually... I think it's kind of charming.

lines: You: Reassignment?
Temporary posting. Long story. Classified. Next question.
*He rubs the back of his head, like an old polo injury.*
You: You really love subway tile, huh?
Love? Ma'am, love is for spaniels. Subway tile is about RESALE. It's white, it's cheap, and nobody in history has ever had a feeling about it. That's the dream.
*He looks at you as if you've just been promoted.*
At last. A woman who understands the market. Everyone I've ever hired was SENTIMENTAL. My last realtor cried at a bay window.
We'll make a fine team, ma'am. I'll give the orders. You'll give... smaller orders.
This? This WAS rose quartz. Hand-mixed by a colorist in Manhattan. She's booked for two years. She cried when I left.
*He presses the side of his head flat against the wall to compare. Same pink. Exactly, precisely the same pink.*
Since my... posting, it has DRIFTED. It now matches the bathroom. I held a tile up to it. I had to lie down on the bath mat for an hour.
We are NOT the same pink. We are, unfortunately, the same pink.
Charming.
*{sfx:TileCrack}Somewhere behind him, a tile cracks. Very slightly.*
Ma'am, I was trained to receive bad news. Nobody trained me to receive bad TASTE.
...Nobody's disagreed with me in a bathroom before. Noted. Logged.
Now. Numbers. My usual flip: two weeks, Swiss Coffee white on every wall, list it on a Thursday, sold by Sunday. Never learn the street name.
Never fall in love with a property, ma'am. First thing my father ever taught me. Second thing was how to fire a nanny.

choices.text: Honestly? That's the dream.
Your father taught you to fire a NANNY?
Never fall in love with a property. What about the people in it?

lines: *He beams.*
A kindred spreadsheet. I knew it the moment you walked in. You have the eyes of a woman who's priced a countertop.
Eleven of them. Consecutively. They'd say no to me, and then they'd be gone. My coach was paid not to say it. The academy didn't dare; Father built them a gymnasium.
So I've never been told no, ma'am. Not and had it stick.
*He says it like a boast. It doesn't quite come out like one.*
*He opens his mouth. Nothing comes out.*
The people in it are... also not to be fallen in love with. Generally. As a rule.
I'll need to check the rulebook. I'll get back to you. Don't look at me like that.
Excuse me, ma'am. It's oh-nine-hundred. Second PT.
*{sfx:Thud}He drops to the bath mat and starts doing push-ups. Fast ones. The light slides across his back like it's a freshly mopped swimming pool.*
Two hundred a day. Fort Bellamy standard. I haven't missed one since my reassignment. I haven't done anything ELSE since my reassignment, but that's beside the point.
*He switches to one arm, purely so you'll notice.*
Don't stare, ma'am. ...Or do. It's been tiled at considerable expense.

choices.text: And what are YOU, exactly?
Need a spotter?
Put a shirt on, soldier.

lines: Me? I'm handling the property. Temporarily attached to it. Between engagements.
*You rest your hand on the cracked tile by the tub. Tyler flinches and touches his temple, where a few small pink tiles have crept up into his hairline like scales.*
Don't— that's— carry on. Cold hands. On the tile. Which I felt. Sympathetically. For the tile.
*He stops mid-push-up. He stays there, perfectly level, like a plank of very expensive bathroom.*
A spotter. Ma'am, nobody has ever... I've always spotted myself. I'll need a moment.
*He gets up and walks to the window very carefully, the way people walk on a wet floor, and stands with his hands clasped behind his back.*
...Count for me tomorrow. Out loud. That's an order. That's a... yes. Carry on.
I don't OWN a shirt, ma'am. Not anymore. I came out of the wall like this.
Shorts. Socks. High-tops. Tile. I've tried putting on a towel. It's white. I can only move pink things. It was a very short war.
*He folds his arms. The grout lines on his biceps flex into perfect diamonds.*
Besides. If you had this, would YOU cover it?
*{sfx:Hum}Out in the hall, the dehumidifier clicks on. Its little green light comes on exactly on the hour.*
*Tyler snaps to attention.*
Now THAT is discipline. On at oh-five-hundred, empties on schedule, never once complains. The only disciplined thing in this house.

choices.text: Did you just salute a dehumidifier?
You're kind of adorable at attention.
Can we get back to MY bathroom?

lines: It's an appliance, ma'am. I'm aware. It has a bucket, a float switch and more self-control than my entire graduating class.
It didn't salute back. Nobody here does. Not the mailman. Not the woman next door with the crossbow. It's a very rude neighborhood.
Adorable? I'm a Whitmore. We're not adorable. We're... imposing.
*He stands up even straighter, which shouldn't be possible for a man that wide.*
...Imposingly adorable. If you insist.
YOUR bathroom. Of course. The deed. Yes.
*{sfx:TileCrack}A tile clicks, sulkily.*
Watch your step on the way out, ma'am. The floor's slick.
*You step very carefully, because he said it so seriously. Too carefully. You wobble and grab the nearest solid thing, which is Tyler's enormous forearm.*
*{sfx:WaterSplash}For one second it's there: cool, smooth, glazed, like tile in the sun. Then your fingers sink straight through, like dipping them in cold bathwater.*
...Steady. I had you. Briefly. That one was a me problem. Don't log it.
*You look down. The floor is bone dry.*
*Tyler is standing at attention by the tub. He doesn't look at you.*
Forty-one minutes, ma'am. I don't own a clock. I counted the drips. Or the sighs. Depending on which of them you were with.
I'm not jealous. Whitmores don't get jealous. We get LITIGIOUS.
*{sfx:TileCrack}A tile clicks. Pointedly.*
Ma'am. You called the tile 'charming' last week.
I've thought about it all week. It's the first time anyone's disagreed with me since 2011. I hated it. I've replayed it forty times. I did my push-ups to it.
Oh. It's YOU. The woman with the deed. To MY bathroom.
Temporary truce. Only because I need your crowbar.
*Tyler has laid out a battle plan on the bath mat. His troops are a pink soap, a pink loofah and a pink rubber duck.*
{sfx:RubberDuck}Ma'am. Today we liberate this bathroom. [Operation Clean Slate|operation]. The duck is you.
Phase one: pull a test tile. Phase two: total demolition. Phase three: white subway and a little wooden sign that says BREATHE.
I've been up since oh-five-hundred. Two hundred push-ups, two hundred sit-ups, a light jog around the tub. My [tan] is really coming along.

choices.text: Yes, sir. Ready for orders.
I'm in charge here, Tyler. Hand me the crowbar.
Who made you general?
Lukey says hi. Well, he said 'tell Pinky the penthouse says hi.'

lines: You: Why a duck?
I can only move pink things, ma'am. It's a condition of my posting. I had to requisition the duck. It was humiliating. The duck was fine about it.
You: Tyler, that's not a tan. That's tile.
It's a GLAZE, ma'am. Very exclusive. Very Mediterranean. You can't buy this. Believe me, I'd have bought it.
*A white grout line runs dead straight across his abs. He flexes so it looks deliberate.*
Outstanding. Finally, someone who respects the chain of command. The duck has been insubordinate all morning.
*{sfx:RubberDuck}He squeezes the duck, sternly.*
*Then he looks at you a beat too long.*
You'd have made a fine cadet, ma'am. Excellent posture. Excellent... crowbar grip.
*He reaches to hand you the crowbar, remembers it isn't pink, and gestures at it with enormous authority instead.*
...Yes. Fine. Carry on. I'll supervise from a strategic distance.
*Under the glaze on his chest, something has gone a shade pinker than tile should be able to go.*
Fort Bellamy did. Youngest cadet captain in its history. At thirteen.
Father donated the gymnasium the same year. Unrelated. Entirely unrelated. Give me the duck.
PINKY.
He lived in my CEILING, ma'am. His 'penthouse.' He dripped on my hair for— for a long time. He looked at my grout and said 'respectfully.' It was NOT respectful.
And now he hums at you. Bon Jovi. I can hear it through the pipes. ...Does he hum at you a LOT? Don't answer that. Crowbar.
*You wedge the crowbar under a tile by the tub and lean on it. Nothing. You lean harder. Nothing. You put your whole weight on it.*
*{sfx:TileCrack}It pops free with a crack.*
Ow.
*Tyler is clutching his ribs. Right where a tile is missing from the wall, a tile is missing from HIM. You can see skin.*
Sympathy pain. Military training. We feel for our equipment.
*{sfx:RubberDuck}The rubber duck topples off the edge of the tub.*
Man down. Leave him. He knew the risks.

choices.text: Tyler. Did that HURT you?
You flinched. That's cute.
Toughen up, soldier.

lines: Hurt? Whitmores don't hurt. We file complaints.
*He rubs his side. Then, absent-mindedly, the back of his head.*
It was like having a tooth pulled by someone with lovely forearms. Look at the back of it.
I didn't flinch. I REACTED. Tactically.
*He's still holding his ribs.*
...Cute, you said? Irrelevant. Strike it from the record. Look at the back of it.
I AM tough. Four winters at Fort Bellamy. We showered in a LAKE.
*He flexes, to prove it. A grout line creaks.*
This is different. Never mind. Look at the back of it.
*The back of the tile is stamped 1957. On the old mortar behind it, someone has written in careful pencil capitals:*
*'SET BY HAL FOR RUTHIE. JUNE 1957. SHE WANTED PINK. BUILT TO OUTLAST US BOTH.'*
*Tyler reads it. Then he reads it again.*
...That's not on the listing.
This is [mud-set|mudset]. An inch of mortar on wire lath. Seventy years and it hasn't moved. I once lost a whole wall of subway in eleven months. The adhesive came from a gas station.

choices.text: Hal and Ruthie. This was somebody's home.
It's good tile, Tyler. Better than anything you'd put up.
Sentiment doesn't sell. Next tile?

lines: You: Since when do you know what mud-set means?
Since... lately. I just KNOW it. The way you know your own handwriting.
*He looks a little unsettled by that.*
Somebody's home. Yes. Every house is somebody's home. That's the whole problem with houses.
*He touches the pencil letters, very gently, with one enormous finger.*
She wanted pink. On purpose. And he built it to last. Imagine someone building you something to last.
Better than— Whitmore Properties has won four regional awards for—
*He looks at the inch of mortar. He looks at the pencil.*
...Three. One was rescinded. Fine. It's good tile. If you tell anyone I said that, I'll deny it in writing.
Exactly. EXACTLY. That's what I'd say. That's exactly what I'd—
*He doesn't finish. He takes the tile from your hand (it's pink; he can) and sets it back in the wall, very carefully, as if it might break. It's lasted seventy years. It won't.*
*The gap in his ribs fills in. He doesn't mention it.*
We'll... keep it on the wall. For now. Tactically.
*You mention, in passing, that the city inspector comes on day thirty.*
*Tyler goes very still. Then he lines up the duck, the soap and the loofah on the edge of the tub and walks slowly down the row, hands behind his back.*
An inspection. Ma'am, why didn't you SAY so. Day thirty. That's a parade. Boots, brass, bearing.
I don't own boots. Or brass. We'll be relying very heavily on bearing.
*He turns to the mirror and salutes it. In the mirror, nobody salutes back. In the mirror, nobody is there at all.*

choices.text: Tyler... the mirror didn't salute back.
Your bearing is fine. Look at you.
It's a house inspection, not a parade.

lines: It's an old mirror. They lose their silver. Happens to the best of us.
Nobody salutes back, ma'am. Not the mirror. Not the mailman, and I've saluted that man every day for— for quite some time.
*He frowns, as if he's lost count of something important. He doesn't look at the mirror again.*
*He flexes. Purely for inspection purposes. Several grout lines creak in harmony.*
Fort Bellamy standard, ma'am. Chin up. Chest out. Chest TILED, currently, but out.
...You were looking at it. That's fine. I'd look at it. I DO look at it.
Everything is a parade, ma'am. Father failed a building once because the doorman slouched.
*He reaches over and corrects your shoulders with two fingers. They pass straight through you, cold as bathwater. He pretends they didn't.*
...Better. Much better. Shoulders back on day thirty. That's an order.
*That night you do the numbers on the edge of the tub. Tyler reads over your shoulder and approves of every one.*
Gut it Monday, tile Tuesday, list it Thursday. That's how I did my last flip. I came in to film the before.
*He trails off, looking at the pencil writing on the wall.*
That's all I remember. The before. I never got to the after.
You're very good at this, ma'am. You remind me of me. That ought to worry you more than it does.

choices.text: Tyler... what happened to you?
Keep me company? I'll do the numbers, you do the judging.
Then let's get to the after. It's all coming out.

lines: Happened? Nothing happened. I'm between engagements.
*He rubs the back of his head.*
It's been a long weekend. It's been a very, very long weekend.
Goodnight, ma'am. Watch your step.
*He sits beside you on the edge of the tub. Perfect posture. His tiled shoulder almost touching yours. Almost.*
Your margins are tight. Your projections are sound. You're... very good at this.
*He clears his throat.*
Goodnight, ma'am. Watch your step.
Outstanding. White. Subway. Basic. Sell.
*{sfx:TileCrack}He says it like a prayer he isn't sure he believes anymore. Behind him, a tile clicks.*
Goodnight, ma'am. Watch your step.
*Tyler is standing with his back to the door. He doesn't turn around. It's a very broad back. He knows.*
You've been with one of THEM. Kitchen or closet. You smell like a sink. Or a sonnet.
You were gone a LONG time. I counted the tiles. Twice. Three hundred and twelve. Both times.
*He turns around. He's been practicing aloof. It isn't working.*
*The power's out, and you've brought a candle. The pink tile glows in it like the inside of a seashell. So does Tyler, from the neck down.*
Power's out. Not my department. I've filed a complaint with the house.
Still. Candlelight. Very flattering. On me. And the tile. Mostly me.
*Tyler sits on the edge of the tub with his high-tops unlaced. For a man who never wears a shirt, it's somehow the most undressed you've ever seen him.*
Ma'am. I've been thinking about Hal and Ruthie. Purely structurally.

The tile remembers things. Don't ask me how. A girl had [chicken pox|pox] in that tub in 1964 and counted every tile. A man hid an engagement ring in the soap dish in 1979. A girl dyed her hair pink in that sink in 1994. Kool-Aid. Good instincts.
In 1987 a woman kept a bottle of wine in here for a [date|brenda] that never happened. She kept it for years.
Seventy years of people. And I wanted a little sign that says BREATHE.

choices.text: You're falling for the tile, Tyler.
You're not who I thought you were.
It's still coming out. You said so yourself.

lines: You: How many tiles did she count?
Three hundred and twelve. She was right. I've checked. Many times. I have a lot of time.
You: Whose date?
No idea. Somebody with excellent taste in wine and terrible luck with dates.
The tile kept watch over that bottle for years. I'd have opened it. I'd have opened it on day two.
Falling? I don't FALL, ma'am. I—
*He goes very still. Something about the word has upset him, and he doesn't know why.*
...I'm reassessing. It's a valuation exercise.
*He looks at you like nobody has ever said that to him and meant it nicely.*
Who did you think I was?
You: A snob with a crowbar.
Accurate. Still accurate. ...But I'm also this, apparently.
I did say so. I say so every day. White. Subway. Basic.
*He doesn't say SELL. He just stops.*
*You tell him you've been researching the house's history for the listing. You searched the address, and something came up.*
*A video. Posted 2024. 'WORST BATHROOM IN AMERICA?! (Flip Day 1).' Three hundred and twelve views.*
*The thumbnail is a huge young man with a rose-quartz pompadour, pulling a horrified face, in this exact bathroom.*

choices.text: Show him the video.
Ask first: 'Tyler, how did you get here?'
You're internet famous, Tyler. Sort of.

lines: *{sfx:RubberDuck}You hold out the phone. He sees himself and stands up so fast he knocks the rubber duck into the tub.*
That's me. That's my GOOD side. Why is my good side on YOUR phone?
...Play it.
Here? The bathroom? I—
*He sees the phone in your hand. He sees the thumbnail. What little of him isn't already the color of the tile goes the color of the tile.*
...Play it.
Three hundred and twelve views? That's not famous, ma'am. That's a GARDEN PARTY.
*Then he sees the thumbnail, and stops talking.*
...Play it.
*On screen, a sweaty, extremely alive Tyler strides into this bathroom, straight from the gym: tank top, pink gym shorts, white crew socks, pink high-tops. He holds his phone at arm's length.*
*'Morning, [Whitmore Nation|nation]. Day one. Leg day, then demo day. Behold: the ugliest bathroom in America. It's Pepto-Bismol. It's the inside of a flamingo.'*
*'This all comes out by Friday. White. Subway. Basic. SELL. Watch your step, this tile is slick as—'*
*{sfx:Bonk}The picture spins. A very loud CLONK. The last frame is the ceiling. It stays on the ceiling for a long time.*
*Underneath, one comment from 2024: 'is he ok'. It has two likes.*
You: Whitmore Nation?
My followers. All three hundred and twelve of them.
...I'm going to be furious about that number in a minute. I'm busy being something else right now.
*The bathroom is very quiet.*
...I'm not between engagements, am I.
I slipped. On the tile. The tile I was calling Pepto-Bismol. On CAMERA. And then I just... stayed. Saluting the mailman.
*He looks down at his shorts. His socks. His high-tops.*
These are the shorts. I've been wearing my LEG-DAY SHORTS for two years. And the tank top... the tank top is now the BATHROOM.
*He touches the back of his head.*
Nobody salutes back because nobody can SEE me. I'm the tile, ma'am. I'm the Pepto-Bismol.

choices.text: Hey. You're still you. Pompadour and all.
Tyler, I'm so sorry.
Three hundred and twelve views is honestly not bad for a bathroom.

lines: *He laughs, short and surprised.*
The pompadour. Yes. They can take my pulse, ma'am. They cannot take my pompadour. They HAVE changed its color, and I will be taking that up with someone.
Don't be. Whitmores don't need sympathy. We need—
*He sits down hard on the edge of the tub. The tub creaks. He's very heavy for a ghost.*
...Actually, I'll take some. A small amount. Don't tell the academy.
Three hundred and TWELVE. One per tile. Even my audience is pink.
*He's laughing. It's slightly hysterical. It's helping.*
But why am I still HERE? Whitmores don't leave business unfinished. Father would have me court-martialed.
...Oh. It's obvious. I never finished the flip. Rip it out, put up the white, sell it, and I'm dismissed. Honorably.
Help me, ma'am. That's an order.
*A beat.*
That's a request. I've never made one before. How did I do?

choices.text: Not bad. But I don't think that's your unfinished business.
Take my hand.
Fine. If that's what it takes.

lines: Then what IS it? I've had everything I ever wanted. Every single thing. That's the Whitmore guarantee.
*He says it like it's the saddest sentence he knows.*
*You reach for him. You expect cold bathwater. Instead your fingers close on something cool, smooth and solid, like glazed tile warmed by the sun.*
...Oh. Hello.
*Maybe it's because you set that test tile back in the wall. Maybe it's something else. He doesn't let go, and he doesn't explain why.*
*He nods. Crisp. Military.*
Outstanding. Thank you, ma'am.
*He doesn't look thrilled. He looks like a man who's just been given exactly what he asked for.*
*When you stand, your hands brush. His doesn't go through yours. It's cool and smooth, like glazed tile warmed by the sun.*
*Neither of you moves. Then he remembers he's old money and shakes your hand, very formally, for no reason at all.*
*{sfx:RadioStatic}The radio in the hall crackles: 'BIG STORM SATURDAY. Heavy rain and flooding expected.'*
A storm. Fine. I've weathered worse. I once weathered a regatta.
Storm protocol, ma'am. Buckets. Sponges. A clear chain of command. I'll be the chain.

choices.text: We'll get through it. Together.
How's Wyatt holding up?
I heard Wyatt finally spoke up.
You're scared of a little rain?

lines: Together. A two-person unit. Smallest regiment in history. Best one.
*He's still holding your hand. Apparently he's decided to.*
Admirably. He's my man. He's done my lighting every morning for— for some time. Never once complained.
Storms make him nervous. Something about New Year's. I told him a Whitmore officer never leaves his batman behind.
The fan went on and off for a full minute. I believe that means he's fine.
Spoke up? He spoke up to ME. I ordered him to keep the bathroom fan running through the storm, and he said NO. To my face. Well, to my extractor fan. I called him insubordinate.
He apologized nine times afterward. But he SAID it.
...He was right. I'm going to tell him so. In a memo.
Scared? Ma'am, I'm glazed ceramic. Water rolls right off me. That's the entire point of me.
*He's quiet for a second.*
...It's the floor I don't trust.
*Late. He walks you to the bathroom door, very carefully, as if the floor might move.*
Thank you, ma'am. For showing me the before.
Watch your step.
*He says it like he means something else entirely.*

*Saturday. The storm hits Heartbreak Lane like it's personal. Water is running down the wall BEHIND the tile, and Tyler is holding the wall up with both hands, every enormous tiled muscle in his back braced. Or trying to.*
{player}!
*It's the first time he's used your name. He's clearly been practicing it in the mirror. The mirror, presumably, didn't answer.*
{player}, report! Where have you BEEN?

*Saturday. The storm hits Heartbreak Lane like it's personal. Water is running down the wall BEHIND the tile, and Tyler is holding the wall up with both hands, every enormous tiled muscle in his back braced. Or trying to.*
Ma'am! Report! Where have you BEEN?
*{sfx:TileCrack}A tile pops off the wall and shatters on the floor. Tyler gasps and grabs his shoulder. There's a bare patch of skin there now, the exact size of a tile.*
The window flashing's gone. Water's getting behind the wall and softening the old mortar. The tiles are coming off one by one, and I can feel every [single one|single].

choices.text: Sorry! The kitchen was flooding. Lukey needed me.
I'm here. Tell me what we do.

lines: You: You can feel them?
Like losing teeth. Very small, very pink teeth. In a storm. While three hundred and twelve people watch.
Not literally. Just the first part.
The KITCHEN. During a CRISIS. You went to the LEAK first.
*{sfx:TileCrack}Another tile drops. He doesn't notice. He's too busy being jealous.*
I'm not upset. I'm SINKING. Literally. ...Fine. Is he all right?

choices.text: He found out he was a person. A real one.
He'll live. Well. You know what I mean. Right now it's you.

lines: A PERSON? The leak? ...That explains the HUMMING. Pipes don't know Bon Jovi.
Well. Welcome to the club. Terrible club. No dress code. Clearly.
*He exhales.*
Good. You're here. That's the main thing.
Listen to me. That's an order. It's over. Let it go. Let it ALL go.
Tomorrow, rip out what's left and put up white subway. Four ninety-nine a square foot. Cheaper, faster, it'll sell. And then I can finally be dismissed.
Seventy years is long enough for anyone. Let the tile go, ma'am. Let ME go.
*{sfx:TileCrack}Another tile cracks off. Behind it, wet and dark but still legible, the pencil: SHE WANTED PINK.*

choices.text: No, Tyler. It stays.
Hal built it to outlast them both. It's going to outlast you too. No.
Stop giving orders and hold this.
You're right. It's coming out.

lines: *You say it once, clearly, the way nobody has ever said it to him.*
*{sfx:Thunder}Tyler stares at you. The rain stares at you. Even the thunder waits a polite second before it goes.*
*{sfx:Thud}You shove a bucket of mortar into his arms. He's solid enough to hold it now. He's so shocked that he does. It's the first time you've seen those arms do something useful.*
You: It stays, Tyler. Hold the bucket.
*You pick up the crowbar. He nods. Crisp. Approving.*
Good. Good. White. Subway. Basic—
*You look at the pencil. HAL FOR RUTHIE. You look at the crack by the tub. You look at him, standing at attention in the rain, waiting to be thrown out like a sample board.*
*You put the crowbar down.*
You: No. Actually, no. It stays.
Did you just tell me NO?
Nobody tells me no! Not eleven nannies, not Madame Fontaine, not Fort Bellamy! I have never been told no in my LIFE. Or... whatever this is!
*He's furious. Properly, magnificently furious. His pompadour is somehow even pinker, and so, faintly, is every tile on the wall.*
You don't get to keep me because it's cheaper! Or because it'll pass inspection! Or because—

choices.text: Because somebody loved it. And because I love it. All of it. Including the part that argues.
Because it's the real fix, and you know it. Built to outlast us.
You told me no one ever said no and meant it. I mean it.
Because I said so.

lines: *He stops mid-shout.*
*Every tile on the wall stops trembling at once.*
Built to outlast— don't quote the WALL at me—
*He stops. He reads the pencil again.*
...Hal would have hated me. And Hal would have been RIGHT.
*He remembers telling you. You can see it land.*
You... remembered that. Eleven nannies and you're the first one who stayed after saying it.
...Carry on. Ma'am. Please.
Because you—
*He opens his mouth. Nothing comes out. Every instinct he has says argue, and for the first time in his life he doesn't know how.*
...Understood.
*So you fight the storm for the tile. You catch them as they fall, and he tells you where each one goes. He knows. He IS them.*
*{sfx:Thunder}Every tile you set back on the wall comes back on him too: a shoulder, a rib, a stripe of pink across his chest, grout lines and all.*
Hold the LINE! Not you, ma'am. [The grout|grout]. Hold the line, grout!
*{sfx:Hum}Out in the hall, the dehumidifier's light turns red. Bucket full. It's an appliance. It has no idea there's a war on. It keeps going anyway.*
*By dawn the wall is back. Every tile set, every line regrouted, every inch sealed. Only the cracked tile by the tub is left.*

choices.text: Mend the crack with gold.
Let him do the last line himself.
Slap some grout on it and call it done.

lines: You: Are you... yelling at yourself?
Fort Bellamy, ma'am. If nobody's shouting at you, you shout at yourself. I've been my own drill sergeant since I was thirteen.
He's very hard on me. He's usually right. Tonight he's ALSO grout.
*You mix gold powder into the epoxy and fill the crack slowly: a thin, bright seam across the pink.*
Gold. You put GOLD on me.
Like the towers. Except nobody paid for this one. You just... did it.
*His hand goes to the back of his head. For the first time, it doesn't seem to hurt.*
*You hand him the grout float. He holds it like a ceremonial sword.*
*He sets the last line himself. It's perfect. Fort Bellamy perfect.*
First thing I've ever fixed instead of flipped. It feels... Whitmores don't have a word for it. We've never needed one.
*{sfx:Squelch}You smear grout over the crack. It's sturdy. It's sealed. It's sort of lumpy.*
...It'll hold. That's the main thing. It's very... you, ma'am.
*He's trying not to criticize it. You can see the effort. It's heroic.*
*Morning. Tyler inspects the wall the way you'd inspect a parade: slowly, hands behind his back, nose an inch from every grout line.*
Restored. Regrouted. Sealed. Let the inspector come on day thirty. Let him bring his clipboard. Let him bring TWO.
*He steps back and salutes the wall. Then, a little awkwardly, he looks at you.*

choices.text: Salute Tyler.
Kiss his cheek.
It's a keeper, Tyler.

lines: *You stand up straight and salute him.*
*He stares at you. Then he returns it, crisp and perfect, and his eyes are suspiciously shiny.*
Somebody saluted back.
*{fx:hearts}{sfx:Kiss}You kiss him on the cheek. It's cool and smooth, like the tile, and it goes a shade of pink no tile has ever achieved.*
That's... not regulation. Do it again sometime. That's an order. That's a request.
A keeper. Me. Kept.
*He tries the word out a few times under his breath, like a new rank.*
*The bathroom glows pink in the morning sun. So does Tyler, faintly, at the edges, the way people do when they're finally finished with something.*
I always got my way. Every nanny, every coach, every deal. And not once did it mean anybody cared.
You told me no. And then you stayed and helped anyway.
I think that was it. The business. I think I'm allowed to go now. ...What are your orders?

choices.text: Stay. That's an order. I'm keeping you too.
I love you. That's why I'm letting you go.
You're a good man, Tyler Whitmore. Dismissed.
That's your call, Tyler.
That's your call, Tyler.

lines: *He blinks.*
That's another no. To me leaving. {player}, you're telling me no AGAIN.
*He's smiling so hard his posture breaks.*
Father said never fall in love with a property. I fell in love with the property AND the owner. He'd be appalled. I'm delighted.
*{fx:hearts}{sfx:Kiss}He kisses you. It's cool and smooth and very, very sure of itself.*

v4_rs2.fxText: The bathroom was pink. So was everything else.
lines: *Much later.*
I still think it looks like Pepto-Bismol. ...I love it. Tell no one.
*{sfx:Kiss}He kisses your hand, very formally. Then, much less formally, he kisses you.*
You told me no, {player}, and you loved me anyway. Nobody's ever done both.
*He steps back, stands at attention and salutes. You salute back.*
Somebody saluted back.
*And then he's gone. All that's left is a gleam on the gold seam by the tub, a little like rose quartz.*
Dismissed. Honorably. Thank you, ma'am.
*He salutes. You salute back. He laughs, astonished.*
Somebody saluted BACK. Log it. Log it TWICE.
*He marches out into the morning light, careful step and all, and doesn't look down once.*
*He thinks about it with his whole posture.*
Then I'll go. Not because I'm ordered to. Because I finally can.
Watch your step, ma'am. ...Actually, never mind. You always do.
*He salutes, and is gone in a gleam of pink.*
My call? Fine. FINE. I'll go.
You kept the tile. You didn't keep it for ME. You kept it for the inspection. I know the difference. I'm a Whitmore.
*{sfx:TileCrack}He marches out with enormous dignity. On the way, one tile on the bottom row clicks very slightly crooked.*
*He did that. Out of spite. ...It's honestly the best tile in the house.*
Ma'am. We've had our briefing. Dismissed.
I'm not jealous of wherever you're going next. I'm keeping a LEDGER.
...You may return next week. I'll be here. I am, regrettably, always here.
{player}! Report. ...No, I know. I just like saying it. Count my push-ups. Then look at that grout. LOOK at it.
*The bathroom is quiet and very pink. The gold seam by the tub catches the light. You salute it. Nobody's watching. You do it anyway.*
*The bathroom is quiet. The vanity light flicks on by itself for a moment, at exactly the angle Tyler liked.*
*One tile on the bottom row is still slightly crooked. You tried to straighten it. It clicked back. You've decided to respect that.*
